Gross margin is defined as net sales less cost of goods sold. Cost of goods sold consists primarily of direct costs of acquiring inventory, including cost of merchandise, inbound freight charges, purchasing costs, and inspection costs for our Branded Products and Healthcare Apparel segments. Cost of goods sold for our Contact Centers segment includes salaries and payroll related benefits for agents. The Company includes shipping and handling fees billed to customers in net sales. Shipping and handling costs associated with out-bound freight are recorded in cost of goods sold. The cost of occupancy and operating the Company’s distribution centers are included in selling and administrative expenses. Gross margin rate is defined as gross margin divided by net sales.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, our Branded Products segment accounted for approximately 64% and 62%, respectively, of net sales.
During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, our Healthcare Apparel segment accounted for approximately 20% and 21%, respectively, of net sales.
During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, our Contact Centers segment accounted for approximately 16% and 17%, respectively of net sales.
At December 31, 2025 and 2024 , the Company had no customer with an accounts receivable balance greater than 10 % of total accounts receivable.

The Company believes that its vast redundant network of suppliers, including its own manufacturing facilities in Haiti, provide sufficient capacity to mitigate most dependency risks on a single supplier.
The Branded Products segment also relies on the supply of other types of raw materials, including plastic, glass and metal.
The Company believes that its redundant network of suppliers, including its own manufacturing facilities in Haiti, provide sufficient capacity to mitigate any dependency risks on a single supplier.
The Branded Products segment relies on raw materials that are principally sourced from China, either directly by BAMKO or its suppliers.

Our success depends upon the continued protection of our trade names, trademarks and other intellectual property rights and we may be forced to incur substantial costs to maintain, defend, protect and enforce our intellectual property rights.

Furthermore, if any of our customers experience a significant downturn in their business, or fail to remain committed to our programs or brands, such customers may reduce or discontinue purchases from us, which has happened.

Our distribution centers and storage locations, as well as those operated by third parties, include computer-controlled and automated equipment and rely on warehouse management systems to manage supply chain fulfillment operations, which means these operations are complicated, require coordination between distribution centers and storage locations and are subject to a number of risks related to cybersecurity, the proper operation of software and hardware, including connections between software and/or hardware, electronic or power interruptions and other system failures.
We rely on information technology systems to process transactions, communicate with customers, manage our business and process and maintain information.
Our Healthcare Apparel segment relies on our manufacturing facilities and warehouses in Haiti for the manufacturing and storage of finished goods.

Future distributions will be declared and paid at the discretion of our Board of Directors, and will depend upon cash generated by operating activities, our financial condition, capital requirements, and such other factors as our Board of Directors deem relevant.
The Company’s primary source of liquidity has been its net income and the use of its Credit Facilities.
The number of shares purchased and the timing of any purchases will depend upon a number of factors, including the price and availability of the Company’s stock and general market conditions.
